Introduction

By using the taktx-client-quarkus wrapper library around the vanilla taktx-client the configuration and initialization of the taktx-client is done automatically. We can use the default Quarkus ways (like application properties) for configuration and the TaktXClient bean is initialized automatically. 

Maven/gradle dependency

To start using it in a Java based application you need to add a gradle/maven dependency to the specific version of the taktx-client which is compatible with your TaktX platform. 

When using maven: 

<dependency>
    <groupId>io.taktx</groupId>
    <artifactId>taktx-client-quarkus</artifactId>
    <version>0.4.0-beta-1</version>
</dependency>

When using gradle:

implementation("io.taktx:taktx-client0-quarkus:0.4.0-beta-1")


During Quarkus initialization the code-base will be scanned for:

  • @Deployment classes automatically upon startup and the corresponding BPMN files will be deployed
  • @TaktWorkerMethod methods upon startup and the corresponding external task topics will be subscribed to

 Also during Quarkus initialization the code-base is scanner for Observer methods which observe InstanceUpdateRecord events. If there are any, a subscription is made to the TaktX engine event-stream and any incoming messages will be published.

For an example, have a look in the GitHub example repo and look specifically for the client-workers-quarkus example.

Deploying BPMN files

To automatically deploy BPMN files we need to add the @Deployment annotation to a Quarkus bean. For example on the main class or on a Configuration bean. 

Starting workers

Workers in Quarkus must be Application scoped beans and also annotated with the @Startup annotation to make sure they are instantiated. By adding @JobWorker annotations on methods the workers are automatically registered and subscribed to the corresponding external task topics.
